report_title: VOXSHIELD Phase 1C.6 — Final AI/ML Phase 1 Analysis & Decision

preferred_model_decision.reason: Demonstrated superior discriminative ranking (ROC-AUC 0.9026 vs RF 0.8106), lower error rate (EER 18.33% vs RF 27.00%), and strong false-alarm suppression (FPR 6.00% vs RF 11.33%) under strict zero-speaker and zero-attack-system leakage. Traditional Random Forest remains preserved as a lightweight fallback (0.59 ms).

1_rf_baseline.training_condition: ASVspoof 2021 DF 2,000-sample benchmark train split (48-D DSP features)
1_rf_baseline.evaluation_condition: Held-out test split (300 samples, speaker-safe, attack systems overlap with train)

2_earlier_indomain_cnn.training_condition: ASVspoof 2021 DF 2,000-sample benchmark train split (Log-Mel + LFCC)
2_earlier_indomain_cnn.evaluation_condition: Held-out test split (300 samples, speaker-safe, frozen val threshold 0.93, attack systems overlap with train)

3_source_disjoint_cnn_val.training_condition: VCC2020 + VCC2018 only (1,400 samples, 97 VCC attack systems, zero A07-A19)
3_source_disjoint_cnn_val.evaluation_condition: VCC validation split (300 samples, 6 disjoint speakers, 95 VCC systems, default threshold 0.50)

4_genuine_unseen_generator_test.training_condition: VCC2020 + VCC2018 only (1,400 samples, 97 VCC attack systems, zero A07-A19)
4_genuine_unseen_generator_test.evaluation_condition: Frozen ASVspoof A07-A19 test manifest (300 samples, 9 disjoint speakers, 13 unseen systems, default threshold 0.50)

comparison_table.evaluation_condition: VCC In-Domain Validation (6 disjoint speakers, theta=0.50)
ASVspoof A07-A19 (13 unseen systems, 9 disjoint speakers, theta=0.50)

interpretation.ranking_discrimination: ROC-AUC improved from 0.8828 to 0.9026 and EER improved from 0.2200 to 0.1833, proving that acoustic phase/spectrogram artifacts learned on VCC voice conversion algorithms transfer effectively to ranking unseen ASVspoof synthesis algorithms.
interpretation.operating_point_shift: At the fixed default threshold (0.50), recall decreased by 22.67% (from 78.00% to 55.33%) because novel synthesis generators output raw probabilities shifted downwards (EER threshold is 0.1873).
interpretation.false_alarms: FPR dropped from 21.33% to 6.00%, driving precision up to 90.22%. The model is highly conservative on unseen real human voices.
interpretation.robustness_caveat: Higher ROC-AUC indicates strong discriminative separation, but does NOT imply universal generalization across all vocoders at a single static threshold.

per_attack_system_summary.false_negative_concentration: 30 of the 67 false negatives (44.8%) were concentrated in just 3 systems: A12, A16, and A17 (waveform filtering, concatenation, and direct neural vocoders). Adding A18 and A19 accounts for 45 of 67 false negatives (67.2%).

streaming_target_100ms_assessment.bottleneck_breakdown: Pure PyTorch forward pass takes only ~6.5 ms (<7% of total). Over 85% of latency stems from disk reading, FFmpeg process invocation, and STFT feature calculation. In-memory streaming PCM buffers in Phase 2 will eliminate file I/O and process spawn overhead.

proven_claims: A genuine neural deepfake detector (MiniAcousticCNN, 93,442 parameters) trains and runs on CPU without requiring an NVIDIA GPU.
Speaker-independent evaluation was strictly verified with 0 speaker overlap across train, validation, and test splits.
Genuine unseen-generator generalization was established with 0 attack-system overlap between training (VCC2020+VCC2018) and evaluation (ASVspoof A07-A19).
MiniAcousticCNN significantly outperforms the traditional Random Forest baseline in discriminative ranking (ROC-AUC 0.9026 vs 0.8106) and error rate (EER 18.33% vs 27.00%).
False-alarm suppression on unseen real human speech is high (FPR 6.00%, Precision 90.22%).
Pure neural inference speed (~6.5 ms / sample) is well within real-time streaming constraints.
unsupported_claims: Generalization to modern commercial closed-source voice cloners (ElevenLabs, OpenAI Voice Engine, CosyVoice, Cartesia, XTTS-v2).
Robustness across 8 kHz telephony codecs (G.711, AMR, GSM, VoIP packet loss).
Robustness across heavy acoustic noise, reverberation, or music background.
Generalization across diverse Indian languages and dialects.
Production-readiness without secondary validation or human-in-the-loop safeguards.
limitations: A07-A19 is an academic benchmark representing 2019 vocoders and synthesis techniques, not 2025/2026 diffusion or zero-shot autoregressive architectures.
Audio evaluated was clean 16 kHz uncompressed FLAC; compressed audio performance remains unquantified.
Default 0.50 threshold suffers from a 44.67% false negative rate on novel waveform concatenation algorithms.
recommended_phase2_work: Phase 2A: Telephony Codec & Channel Augmentation (evaluate 8 kHz downsampling, G.711 A-law/mu-law, and AMR).
Phase 2B: Commercial Clone & Multilingual Data Collection (create an evaluation set with ElevenLabs, CosyVoice, and Indian languages).
Phase 2C: Threshold Calibration & Multi-Tier Confidence Scoring (calibrate operating threshold to lower FNR while maintaining FPR <= 10%).
Phase 2D: Streaming In-Memory Feature Pipeline & ONNX Export (replace disk I/O with circular PCM buffers and export MiniAcousticCNN to ONNX for production runtime integration).
